candidate.answerReason: Distributing gives four terms, and x^2 times x^3 equals x^5.

methods.label: Distribute the factors
methods.explanation:
Multiply each term of the first factor by both terms of the second factor. The product \(x^2x^3\) has five factors of \(x\), so it equals \(x^5\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
(1+x^2)(1-x^3)
&=1-x^3+x^2-x^2x^3\\
&=1+x^2-x^3-x^5.
\end{aligned}
\]
The result is \(1+x^2-x^3-x^5\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: Termwise polynomial multiplication and the positive-integer exponent rule are elementary school algebra.
